close_reason: O(1) refcount index replaces O(N) recompute. task_lists_with_tasks: HashSet<Id> → task_list_refcount: HashMap<Id, u64>. Inner::inc_task_ref / dec_task_ref helpers maintain the count incrementally at each Task create/update/destroy/seed site; the change_object loop now does the change directly instead of scanning every Task per mutation. dec_task_ref removes entries at refcount=0 so task_list_has_tasks reads contains_key. cargo fmt + clippy + workspace test (2190 passing) green. The 15 integration tests in tests/tasks_tests.rs include task_list_set_destroy_with_tasks_returns_error which exercises the refcount path end-to-end.
description:
memory.rs:196-210 rebuilds the entire task_lists_with_tasks index by scanning every Task in the account on every Task create / update / destroy call (memory.rs:643, 701, 731, 793). For an account with N tasks, every mutation is O(N).

At N=100k the rebuild dominates the mutation cost; at N=1M it makes the reference impl unusable for any soak / load test. The 'reference impl' framing makes this defensible-as-is, but it actively teaches the wrong pattern to a contributor who lifts memory.rs as the starting point for a database backend.

The index is trivially incrementally maintainable: on create with taskListId T → set.insert(T); on update where taskListId changed from T0→T1, set.remove(T0) if no other task references T0, set.insert(T1); on destroy where taskListId was T, remove T if no other task references T. The 'no other task references T' check is itself O(N) unless a refcount is also maintained — refcount is the right shape and trivial: a HashMap<Id, u64> with one increment/decrement per mutation.

Recommended remediation: replace the HashSet<Id> field with a HashMap<Id, u64> refcount, drop recompute_task_lists_with_tasks, and increment / decrement at create / destroy / update sites. The task_list_has_tasks check becomes 'refcount >= 1'.
title: MemoryBackend.recompute_task_lists_with_tasks is O(n) per mutation
